newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas trade scrappy, interest in winter only.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas trade scrappy, interest in winter only.

text.p: Trade on IPE natural gas futures was thin and scrappy on Friday, with the market lacking clear direction and the big traders that dominated play in the last couple of days now absent, brokers said.
"We saw big volumes over the past couple of days and now we're back to normal," said one. "There has been concern expressed by the smaller players over manipulation of the market."
IPE prices strengthened on Thursday as large players in the over-the-counter (OTC) market came in to buy up futures in an effort to push up market levels.
Brokers noted that the illiquidity of the IPE contract offered players the opportunity to shift prices on relatively small volumes.
"The oil markets went through this as do all fledgling markets," said one broker.
"We need to see at least 10 or 15 new players to come into the market," he added.
Trading volumes totalled 220 lots, down from Thursday's 530 lots. Open interest stood at 3,115 lots at the end of Friday's session.
Once again, January and February were the focus of interest, with each month gaining 0.10 pence a therm (p/th) to end the day at 16.40 p/th and 16.50 p/th respectively.
Traders said that the award of Transco's annual storage tender left many players empty handed and sent them into the market for winter gas.
"There's still good buying in the first quarter. People believe that they may be able to sell as high as 20 pence when the winter comes," a dealer said.
But fourth quarter months eased lower, while the summer months remained more or less untraded.
"No one wants to take a punt on the summer. It's hanging on the cusp of 10 pence," said a broker.
